items.title: William Ballariel Interview, 1959-10-02
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Frank; Frank is only mentioned by the interviewer in the question 'You're pregnant, Frank.'

ctx.x: Yeah, they're mixed with French and all. Now, my mother, I've been there as I can learn, she came from down in Nassau somewhere, and she spoke French good. My mother was really speaking French. And her mother, she came from Bordeaux, France, my wife's mother. Bordeaux, France. And that's it, they spoke French good. But the younger ones, the people of Mononville Island, they kept the broken French, I believe. They called it the regular Creole talk down there, and they didn't speak it down there yet. But in the…
You're pregnant, Frank. We certainly enjoyed hearing about the old times. And I was going to ask you about those early string bands. Did they have any drums in there?

Well, they'd have a, they'd have a, what they call a, they'd have a drum with a cymbal on it and a trap. They'd call it a trap drum, you see. Now one man would use both. He'd use his foot with the bass drum, it wouldn't be very loud, you see. And he'd use his hand with the snare drum. They had the drums, yeah, in the orchestra. They have them right now, you see. They got them yet.
